name: Automation (webdriver) flag
plain: True when the browser is being driven by Selenium, Playwright, Puppeteer or similar.
meaning: Tells a site a script, not a person, may be on the page. Bot defenses use it with other tells (missing plugins, headless UA) to block or challenge scrapers and agents.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell if Selenium, Playwright, or Puppeteer is controlling the browser
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Check whether the browser says it is automated
Combine it with other clues like a headless label
Block, slow, or challenge likely scrapers and AI agents
cannot: Be sure; bot makers can hide the flag
See what the script is doing
Tell a good script from a bad one
Show true when you browse by hand

story.what_it_is: A simple true or false that says a script, not a person, is driving the browser.

marketing.name: Navigator.webdriver
marketing.pitch: Docs say this flag is true when the browser is controlled by WebDriver automation.

story.for_you: You never see it. In an ordinary browser it says false and nothing changes. If you run an automation tool, some sites will challenge you.
story.for_makers: It is the cheapest bot test: one line of code. Defences use it with other tells like missing plugins and headless user agents. It catches lazy scrapers but not skilled ones.

use_cases.example: A web firewall serves a challenge page to clients with the flag set.
A concert ticket seller blocks scalper scripts that run in automated browsers.
A multiplayer browser game bans automation that plays for you.
An ad network refuses to count ad views from automated browsers.
A traffic tool removes automated visits so your numbers are cleaner.
A QA engineer sees the flag in a test run and sets sites to test mode.
A flight site stops fare scraping bots by challenging automated browsers.

technical_bounds: Does not identify who runs the automation

linkedin.how: Collected as automation flag and framework detection. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
